single_root_cause: The running backend was still executing the old login path while two PostgreSQL containers were attached to the same console_postgres_data volume and the same console_postgres network alias. During /auth/login, the old synchronous lockout-column reflection hit PostgreSQL catalog/index error 'column is not in index', returning HTTP 500. The frontend surfaced that failure as a credentials-style sign-in error.
responsible_layer: runtime deployment and database container topology, with a backend login-path resilience gap
not_the_cause: The configured owner user exists in the current production database.
The configured owner password matches the stored owner password hash.
The rebuilt frontend no longer uses /auth/me as the login success criterion.
RBAC core engine was not involved.

remediation.detail: SQLAlchemy reflection errors now degrade to lockout columns unavailable instead of failing login.

remediation.action: Rebuilt and recreated active backend/frontend containers

remaining_operational_note: Single-login responses now return successfully and consistently. Occasional latency variation remains due to Argon2 password verification CPU cost; this is distinct from the previous false 401/500/login-state problem.
